newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end gently up in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end gently up in thin trade.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up slightly Monday in thin trade, lifted by the region's slight upswing and a gentle rebound of benchmark Telefonica del Peru, brokers said.
Volume was seen continuing low Tuesday as investors, particularly from abroad, were expected to remain sidelined due to the economy's slower-than-expected growth, they added.
Monday, the General Index edged up 0.3 percent to 1,436.6 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index rose 0.3 percent to 2,039.7 points, according to preliminary figures.
Trade was "really apthetic," said Jennifer Bracale of local brokerage Provalor. "The rise came because of a recovery in Telefonica and a general upward swing in the region."
In 1,088 trades, volume was 25.7 million soles ($10.0 million), boosted by an 11 million sol cross-trade within the same brokerage of tin-miner Minsur, brokers said.

In general, players have been sidelined for the last few months because they believe the economy will grow no more than 2.5 percent this year, down from the government's six percent estimate at the beginning of 1996.
Monday, Telefonica closed up 1.19 percent at 5.11 soles in volume of 1.14 million shares, according to preliminary figures.
Electricity distributor Luz del Sur, in which the government is selling a 30 percent stake this month, closed down 2.55 percent at 3.44 soles in volume of 164,000 shares.
Minsur's stock adjusted to a share split, bringing its price down 56.29 percent to 9.90 soles from 22.60 soles.
